01.title: She Got Life for Murder. The 'Blood' Was Sound-Deadener. #Shorts
01.next_task: human-style frame review recorded in production_manifest.json 'editorial_review'
01.episode_summary: Azaria Chamberlain (Uluru, 1980-2012): a mother jailed for life on 'baby's blood' that was factory sound-deadener; a jacket found by chance freed her; a 2012 inquest confirmed a dingo took her daughter.

defects_found_and_fixed: hand-to-face gesture read as a wave -> rebuilt as hand-to-mouth
judge/coroner too small at the bench (scale 0.42 -> 0.5)
verdict shot opened on an empty wall -> tighter start on the bench, Lindy revealed by the tilt down
frontal walk read as a kick -> 3/4 walk with shorter stride
magnifier hidden by the bench -> aimed above it
label boxes collided with the judge's head -> bench figures moved off-centre
night search lacked tension -> subtle handheld camera
animation_director.notes: Character continuity holds across shots by construction (same characters/figures/*.json): Lindy (court/release outfits), Michael, judge, scientist recur unchanged. Remaining limit: 2D cut-out rig, rigid limbs, simple hands.

checks: narration identical to the reviewed, sourced v1 script (tests/test_cinematic.py)
every shot's claims are 'established' with >=2 sources (shot_manifest validation)
no depiction of Azaria, the dingo, violence or blood; dashboard 'spray' drawn dark brown
real people are illustrated representations, not likenesses; others generic
every reconstruction tagged ILLUSTRATION; jacket shot tagged NOT THE ACTUAL JACKET
no invented dialogue; prosecution case labelled as a claim; no 'declared innocent'

retention_strategist.hook: 0-3.6 s: Lindy in the dock under the judge, 'A mother was jailed for life for murdering her baby', gavel hit; 2.9 s later the 'NOT BLOOD' reversal.
retention_strategist.pacing: 14 shots, average 6.0 s, longest 10.7 s (science reveal, three staged callouts); payoff in the 2012 finding; memorial close with fade.
defects_found_and_fixed: captions overflowed the Shorts UI (right 1039 px, bottom 1563 px) -> 800 px safe width at y 1380, long words scaled

software_test_engineer.result: 16/16 QA checks pass; 87 unit tests pass
defects_found_and_fixed: motion-energy metric could not tell a slideshow from animation (v1 also passed) -> kept only as a frozen-picture detector; character action now probed from the renderer
test module name collision between the two make_episodes.py files -> loaded by path
self-matching pgrep in a wait loop -> waits on the real PID

03.title: A Teen Was Found in a Pop Star's Tesla. Where the D4vd Case Stands Now #Shorts
03.next_task: Before publishing: re-check the 19 Oct 2026 hearing status; then upload (YouTube: altered/synthetic content = Yes).
03.episode_summary: The D4vd case (Los Angeles, ongoing): remains found in a Tesla registered to the singer; his arrest, the charges (allegations), his not-guilty pleas, the July holding order, the change of counsel, and the next hearing. Presumption of innocence stated; no real person depicted.

soundtrack.engine: pipeline/score.py (original, procedural; no samples or third-party audio)
soundtrack.sections: A hook s01-s02 · B investigation s03-s05 · C questions s06-s09 · D cliffhanger s10-s11 (impact on 'trial' at 70.4 s) · E exit s12
soundtrack.licence: original work generated in this repository; no attribution required (see docs/CREDITS.md)

editorial_review.method: rendered artefact: 24 extracted frames + 12 re-render frames, measured audio (pipeline/audio_qa.py), offline ASR transcript; no human listening test was possible in this environment

findings.note: Hook lands: tow yard, smell, remains, then the registration card and D4VD caption by ~9 s.
Press-room shot near-static for 10 s (only card rows change).
Hills shot dark and static for 9 s; house partly under the timeline card in preview.
Restrained build: section phone-band medians A -41.9, B -45.4, C -43.5, D -40.9, E -41.8 dB; drops at 6 s and 51 s are intentional.
Cliffhanger impact lands on 'trial'; unresolved cluster carries into the exit.
Rain effect bed held at ~-32 dBFS and was chopped in the last 20 ms while the picture faded; the ending check (250 ms average) missed it.
First word at 0.31 s (intended 0.25), gap bed 14.5 dB under speech, no holes; -14.2 LUFS, TP -1.6 dBTP, mono 0 LU.
Defence quote card should say the lawyers were former counsel (they withdrew 31 Aug 2026).
All narration attributed and sourced (13 claims, >=2 sources each); 'pleaded not guilty', 'not a verdict', 'presumed innocent' present; next date 19 Oct as scheduled 31 Aug, re-searched 2026-10-11.
Two longest shots back to back at the midpoint with little motion: drop-off risk.
Charge card text 26-29 px is small on a phone.

fixes_applied: master tail fade in pipeline/mixdown.py (all score and effects end with the picture) + stricter ending check (last 50 ms < -48 dBFS) + regression test
press room: keyed push-in wide -> medium -> close, handheld; podium extended to the floor
hills: stronger push toward the house, handheld; house moved clear of the timeline card
Case Files 01/02 re-mixed with the same fix and re-verified

executive_producer.note: Mid-video shots now move (push-ins); every scene adds a new fact; ending lands on the next hearing and the presumption of innocence.

composer_sound_designer.note: Score sections and drops unchanged; exit fades with the picture. Remaining: the build is deliberately restrained; louder D section is a taste call, not changed.

audio_engineer.note: Last 50 ms -95.5 dBFS, last 250 ms -66.2 dBFS; all 10 audio checks pass; full decode clean; A/V within 58 ms.

legal_factual.note: Former-counsel attribution added; no allegation presented as fact; no graphic or tabloid detail; no real person depicted.

mobile_retention.note: Captions inside the safe area (x 105-975, y 1281-1483); cards readable; first 10 s strong.

outstanding: No human listening test was possible here; levels are measured, not heard.
The 19 Oct 2026 hearing could be continued after publication; re-check the docket before posting and update the closing line if it moves.
ASR mishears proper names (Rivas, Elsinore) - the narration itself uses the correct names.
